comment_data.body: Not the author or maintainer, but just wanted to notify you that mini.nvim as of now support 0.9 version of neovim properly atleast until nvim 0.12 is released which might most probably be released this december. You can read the `Supported Neovim versions` section in MAINTAINING.md for mini.nvim. And afaik, vim.uv was introduced in 0.10. So if we go ahead with this PR, it is essentially breaking the compatibility of 0.9. So I highly doubt this is a change which we should do in mini.nvim atleast until 0.12 is released.

Thank you for the suggestion!

As @231tr0n said, 'mini.nvim' still aims to support Neovim=0.9, so a simple rename is a breaking change.

Doing `(vim.uv or vim.loop)` each time or once per file (like `local uv = vim.uv or vim.loop`) adds unnecessary churn, because these renames are already planned to do after Neovim=0.9 support is dropped. There is no harm or side effects in using `vim.loop` for now.

Closing as "it is planned for after Neovim=0.9 support is dropped".
